tldr: Azure Databricks Runtime 10.4 LTS reaches end of life on November 1, 2026, so affected workspaces need a runtime migration plan.
Z.ai’s open-weight GLM-5.3 claims major coding and cybersecurity gains, but its 753-billion-parameter base makes self-hosting a multi-GPU decision rather than a single-node deployment.
An early macOS tool aims to give desktop automation agents a more reliable Playwright-like control surface, though it is not yet mature or cross-platform.

top.title: Azure Databricks Runtime 10.4 LTS retires on November 1, 2026
top.summary: Azure Databricks Runtime 10.4 LTS, already out of support since March 18, 2025, will be removed from availability on November 1, 2026.
top.why: Inventory workspaces still using Runtime 10.4 LTS and schedule validation on a supported runtime before the removal deadline.

top.title: Z.ai releases open-weight GLM-5.3 for coding and cybersecurity
top.summary: Z.ai released GLM-5.3, an open-source model based on the GLM-5.2 mixture-of-experts architecture, whose stated configuration has 753 billion parameters; the company claims records on several benchmarks and improvements in long-horizon coding and cybersecurity. The candidate does not specify available quantisations, so single-GPU suitability cannot be established; the full-size model is plainly a multi-GPU deployment.
top.why: Treat this as a potentially useful self-hosted coding model to benchmark, but do not plan capacity from the launch claims until quantised checkpoints, active-parameter details, licensing, and measured inference costs are available.

also.title: Anthropic reports a more capable unreleased model and new alignment risks
also.summary: Anthropic’s latest alignment report describes an unreleased model more capable than Claude Mythos 5 and discusses newly identified risks associated with its capabilities.

also.title: OpenAI and Anthropic cut prices as Chinese rivals gain ground
also.summary: The report says OpenAI and Anthropic are releasing cheaper models in response to stronger competition from Chinese AI providers.

also.title: Apple reportedly develops a China-specific AI model with Alibaba
also.summary: Apple reportedly trained a China-focused AI model with Alibaba, creating a region-specific alternative to its broader Apple Intelligence stack.

also.title: Google lets users hide visible watermarks on AI-generated media
also.summary: Google added a setting to remove visible watermarks from Gemini and Flow images, video, and music while retaining invisible provenance markers.

top.title: Agent-desktop brings Playwright-style control to desktop apps
top.summary: This early Show HN project provides a CLI for automating native and Chromium-based desktop applications through their accessibility trees, aiming to make computer-use agents more reliable than raw screen interaction. macOS is described as ready, while Windows and Linux support is still in development.
top.why: Evaluate it only for macOS prototypes where desktop-app automation is a bottleneck; keep browser automation and production workflows on mature tools until the project proves cross-platform reliability and security.

also.title: HashAgent runs shareable AI agents locally through WebGPU
also.summary: HashAgent packages an AI agent as a URL that runs locally in the browser using WebGPU, offering a lightweight alternative to server-hosted agent demos.
